title: Do not impose walltimes on physics-limited stages: an unlimited partition gains nothing from one
symptom: A 512-q Si G0W0 stage was submitted with --time=12:00:00 chosen from an SCF-based estimate. It was still in the Sigma pass (i_tau 8/16) when Slurm killed it at 09:04, after 8 h 19 min, with no KS/EXX/GW band tables written - all of that compute was lost.
root_cause: The stage runtime is set by the physics (q-points x frequency points x bands), not by a schedule the operator can predict in advance. On a partition whose limit is infinite a walltime therefore has no upside and one clear downside: it converts a slow-but-finishing run into a total loss.
minimal_fix: Omit resources.walltime_minutes from the execution profile (or set it to 0). The profile loader normalises a missing value to 0 and the stage template then emits no #SBATCH --time, so Slurm applies the partition limit. Only state a walltime on a partition that requires one, and then size it from a measured per-task time x task count, never from another stage's runtime.
validation: squeue shows TIME_LIMIT = UNLIMITED for the stage, the stage script contains no #SBATCH --time line, and the run reaches COMMAND_COMPLETED instead of dying on the limit.
avoid: Do not 'be safe' with a walltime on an unlimited partition, and do not derive it from the SCF (39 min) when LibRPA is 20x longer.
source: job 1895 killed by TIME LIMIT at 2026-10-29T09:04 (12 h) versus job 1902 submitted with TIME_LIMIT UNLIMITED on the same run.
